title: Registration and orientation
summary: Orientation is delivered once per session and again after a context restart (SessionStart clear or compact on Claude and Codex, preCompact on Cursor). Each attempt is claimed under a per-session lock, so parallel hooks such as Cursor's concurrent postToolUse deliver it once; an undelivered request settles its claim lost for the next event to repair. In the Cursor IDE, the first chat in a newly opened window fires no sessionStart, so its first beforeSubmitPrompt delivers the block. It confirms delivery only after context emission. Each harness writes the exact merged and budgeted context body's UTF-8 byte_count and SHA-256 into the existing delivered marker, without storing the body. Receiving QA reads the marker on its retained host through qa mission host-command, including Cursor where transcripts omit hook bodies. Emission evidence remains distinct from native receiving proof, which waits for released QA. Registration reports registered, exists, skipped with a reason, or refused with a named code. Refusals remain fail-open and surface on stderr and in SessionRegistrationRefused. The authoritative registration write persists the first prompt independently of orientation markers; roster reads hide true probes while an explicit session read returns their audit row marked probe.
